title: Breville BES980BTR The Oracle Espresso Machine, Black Truffle $1,887 (RRP $3,399) Delivered @ Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Breville BES980BTR The Oracle Espresso Machine, Black Truffle $1,887 (RRP $3,399) Delivered @ Amazon AU

[Kawaii] Is this better than Dual Boiler?
Any pros and cons?
[High] Pro : grinder is included
Con: grinder is included (higher cost, harder to repair, more parts to break down)
[hydration station] with the grinder as one you cook the beans before they are ground
[Whiplash] Grinder is trash. Hand grinder like the K7 and an aldi drill do better and more for your coffee.
[ATTS] Whats ur opinion the breville smart grinder
[cyberbastion] @ATTS: I'm interested in this too. The integrated grinder on my Breville machine is becoming unreliable, so I've decided to switch to a dedicated coffee grinder.
[mousie] @ATTS: Loved mine. Now have a Sunbeam grinder and it's totally fine
[ATTS] @mousie: Nice thanks
Btw would u know which grinder mcdonald's use to grind the oreo in their mcflurry?
[freefall101] Pros - it has a grinder in it too, plus the auto-tamp stuff
Cons - it costs more
[60beetle60] Another pro, I like the auto milk froth, set up preferred temperature before hand and its one push of the lever and it stops at the desired temperature. My 2yr old loves making himself babychino's with our oracle
[wfdTamar] I've had an Oracle for 12 years. Better if you want easy. The dual boiler BS920 is better if you want to master technique. Grinder being separate you could either buy a better grinder than the 'standard' match - the Smartgrinder, or upgrade the grinder later.
I don't use it now as I have a Rancilio Silvia with Gaggimate Pro which is more fun to fiddle with.
[Shiny Mew] Gaggimate Pro is an interesting gadget. Would the combo you now use be far too complicated for someone who has never used an espresso machine before?
[wfdTamar] It depends on you. If you're comfortable using tools and pulling a basic coffee machine to bits. First you have to install the Gaggimate. Then using it is more complicated than say a Breville Bambino, but there's good online help. You could start with a machine capable of having the Gaggimate installed, but not install that until you had your coffee making technique worked out.
It can also be a cheap way to get a good machine. There are always used Silvias (or Gaggia Classics) available used.
Have a look at Decent Espresso (A$5500-6000) - this is the machine that Gaggimate is trying to be and really for the money, it does a good job.
[willyroo] Not quite.
I had one of these at a contract role, BSB + SGP at home.
With the BDB I usually pull a better shot, using Aldi Medium as the control bean.
Milk texturing - BDB much better.
[Aminn] My best experience from Facebook market, got a brand new one in box for $500, 7 years ago, still going strong
[huntabargain] And why did someone sell it brand new in a box for $500, was it stolen?
[Aminn] IDK, He said I won it in raffle at out gulf club, he gave me his number as well so in case I could follow up and get receipt for warranty purposes
[Schumi5] Same price at Harvey Norman but get additional 10% back in gift cards.
https://www.harveynorman.com.au/breville-the-oracle-espresso…
[browser] It's currently $1,999 from Breville , there's an Amex 6% back if you have it.
Works out to $1,879 if you prefer to buy from Breville and get the bonus pack. It seems everywhere gets 1kg free bean by registering, but bonus pack is exclusive to Breville.
[BargainsGrabber] $1799.10 delivered with the 10% off code
BrevFuture10-u1hVgPNF8Q
[browser] Wow! $1,691 when combined with Amex. Plus 1kg of bean and bonus pack (puck sucker, 500g canister, and 2 x 200ml double wall glasses).
[trevor99] 1kg of beans is such a tiny percentage of the price, yet they pump it. Marketing - everyone loves the aroma of freshly ground beans.
[Lifeline] And the beans you'll get will be stale af.
[miura] Amazing machine, have had one for just over 8 years now and use it daily for 3-4 coffees. Avoid over spending on fancy touch screen machines and get this one instead. Much better built. Parts are cheap and easy accessible. Most repair shops charge fixed labour of $180 + parts.
[Shiny Mew] Given how long it’s been on the market, if it’s superseded soon will that cause repairs and parts to become more expensive and harder to obtain?
[theunwiseone] Does anyone know how the new Ninja Autobarista pro compares to this? Understand they are two very different machines but just curious of people’s experience.
[rbrtsluk] I wouldn’t recommend the black truffle as we had the brushed aluminium right also years but the black truffle lost its coding after about six months they all do it
[repeat] I would prefer the current deals on the dual boiler for $1212 from the good guys (price beat) or HN for $1222 with (10%) $122 in GC, then get a much better grinder like a DF64.
Built in grinder is convenient, but has drawbacks due to integral nature and potential flavour exploration. Built in tamping is something I wouldn't personally use, and to me appears (together with the grinder) to be another thing to go wrong/disrupt, same as the auto milk texturing - both may help if you don't want to work on technique, but will insulate you from awareness of the process.
background: have had a few dual boilers since 2014, DF64 1st gen since early 2022 and recently made a cheap burr upgrade with good results.
